questions.q: What makes a miscellaneous receipt different from a standard receipt?
options: A miscellaneous receipt can only be entered by a manager
A miscellaneous receipt is always for a smaller dollar amount
A miscellaneous receipt distributes cash straight to GL accounts and never touches a customer's open balance
A miscellaneous receipt cannot be reversed
questions.explain: Miscellaneous receipts record cash with no connection to a customer balance, distributing directly to General Ledger accounts instead.

questions.q: Which type of Receivables Activity must be assigned to a miscellaneous receipt?
options: Adjustment
Miscellaneous Cash
Late Charge
Write-off
questions.explain: A miscellaneous receipt requires a Receivables Activity of type Miscellaneous Cash, which determines the GL account on the credit side.

questions.q: On a miscellaneous receipt, what typically forms the debit side of the accounting entry?
options: The customer's accounts receivable account
The cash account tied to the remittance bank account
A suspense account that is never cleared
The sales revenue account
questions.explain: The debit side of a miscellaneous receipt is almost always the cash account for the remittance bank account, same as any receipt.

questions.q: What is a distribution set used for on a miscellaneous receipt?
options: Splitting a standard receipt across multiple customers
A reusable template of GL accounts and percentages for a recurring type of receipt
Setting the approval limit for write-offs
Generating a customer statement
questions.explain: A distribution set is a predefined, reusable template of accounts and split percentages, useful for a recurring type of miscellaneous receipt.

questions.q: Which of these is a typical example of a miscellaneous receipt?
options: A customer paying their open invoice in full
A customer paying two invoices with one check
Interest earned on the company's operating bank account
A credit memo issued for returned goods
questions.explain: Interest income has nothing to do with any customer's open balance, which is exactly the kind of cash event a miscellaneous receipt is built for.
